utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stringer, do you have anything to address the Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, we're ready to proceed with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no protective measures with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You're correct, Mr. President. The witness has requested that he has a pseudonym, but no other protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there's no objections from Defence counsel. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, would you please stand up. Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is going to show to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It seems that we have some problem with the sound. We don't hear the witness. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good afternoon. Thank you. There is interference, which very noisy. I don't know if you can hear it, but it is impossible to follow, all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mark, can you hear me? Would you please say something. I'm sorry, we cannot hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, you may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I begin, I could inform the Trial Chamber of the relevant parts of the indictment, which are paragraphs 9 and 11 of background; paragraphs 15, 16, and 17 regarding superior authority; the general allegation of widespread and systematic campaign, paragraph 21; paragraphs 25, 27, 28, and 34 of count 1; counts 2 through 5 regarding forced labour; and paragraphs 46 and 50 of counts 9 through 12, which relate to torture and beatings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would you please inform us about his pseudonym, please, for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I believe that the pseudonym for this witness will be TT.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me and see me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Before I start asking you questions, I can inform you that the Trial Chamber has granted your request to use a pseudonym during your testimony so that you will be called "Witness TT", and I will refer to you with that pseudonym during your testimony, and I ask you not to say anything that would tend to identify you to those who are listening and watching today. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am picking up a fair amount of background in my headphones. I can proceed, but I don't know if anyone else wants to proceed with it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] Every one of us also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Really.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I noticed the Defence microphone is on also, maybe that would...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may try.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, but the technical booth said turn the remote witness -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: For everyone, the audio remote witness dial should be turned down, and everyone should otherwise control the volume with the button that's normally used. Is that correct? Okay, I'll attempt to start.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, I apologise for the trouble. There's a piece of paper which Mr. Dubuisson is holding, the man seated next to you, and I would ask at this time that you look at that piece of paper and tell us if that piece of paper contains your true and correct name.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We either cannot hear the witness or we have very strong interference. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, from the English interpretation booth, I have been informed that the interpreters are having difficulty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have been informed that the Defence should use the volume control, and the English speaking booth should also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Another thing is that I wonder whether we could lower the lights in this courtroom so that we could see the picture more clear.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We would like to do a test just to make sure.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Witness needs to say something so that we can see if we can pick up his voice.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can the witness please say something, his pseudonym perhaps.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If we take the remote control off, then we cannot hear the witness. If we put on the remote control up, then the interference is too strong, and we, again, cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you were trying to tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps it may be best to just a short break until this is sorted out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll adjourn for 10 minutes. --- Break taken at 3.14 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope everything is okay. Mr. Stringer, you may try.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me just ask you a couple general questions about your background. Are you a Bosnian Muslim who was born and raised in the village of Sovici in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in April of 1993, were you a member of the village defence or the Territorial Defence in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And at that time, was it part of your job to man a position near Sovici at a place called Duga Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you at this location, Duga Grude, on the morning of 17 April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, I was first at the Mackovica, and that same morning, I moved to Duga Grude before the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned an attack. Can you tell us what happened, at what time the attack started and how you became aware of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: It happened on the 17th of April in the morning sometime between 7.00 and half past 7.00. We saw troops moving towards our positions, and I went to a place called Duga Grude. And then shells began to fall on the positions. And Jablanica was shelled for two days, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, tell me, what time did the shelling begin when you were at Duga Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Around 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was that in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you able to tell from your position where the shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: The shells came from the direction of Risovac and Vozdac, and from down there, from Sovicka Vrata, from that area around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At that time were you aware or did you know what army or what units were deployed in those places that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No, we didn't know that. We knew that it was the HVO, but not what part of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, how long did the shelling continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Until afternoon, until half past 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And where were you during the time that the shelling was taking place on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: On the positions at Duga Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what you did then when the shelling stopped that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We withdrew to the woods, which is below our positions, and waited for the night to fall. And then to move on to the village of Munikoze.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you withdrew into the woods, were you able to see the village of Sovici or any part of it after you had gone into the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the upper part of the village, whole of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Would that be what's called Gornja Mahala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What were you able to see? What was happening in Gornji Mahala from your position in the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We saw HVO men calling out our women and children to go to the school -- or rather, to the bus. And they were already entering the hamlet of Cilici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where is the hamlet of Cilici located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: It is to the right, in the direction of Obruc.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is it in Gornji Mahala or another part of the village, or are you able to give us a better idea for those of us who don't know the village well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, it is Gornji Mahala. It is a hamlet right above the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] We lost the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, we lost the picture, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please see to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I've just been informed that we are connected but they need to check something, so it will take just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It appears we have the picture back, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, witness, just before we were interrupted, you were telling us about what you saw from your position in the woods. Then what did you do that -- on the rest of the day, which is the 17th of April? Where did you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. go? Where did you spend that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We spent the night -- or rather, that day we headed for Munikoze and that is where we stayed one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the following day, the 18th of April, tell us what you did on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Then, from Munikoze we started for the village of Parcani, which is also in the Prozor municipality, and there we spent another night.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, by this time, can you tell us, were you accompanied by any of your comrades from the Territorial Defence or the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. We were nine altogether. That is 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have one question for the witness in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, can you tell us what you did, then, you and the rest in your group, on the next day, which would have been the 19th of April, and where did you spend the night of the 19th of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, witness, the following day, the 20th of April, can you tell us what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: On the 20th of April, we only walked about two kilometres down from the place where we had spent the night and by a stream, we were to wait for the night to fall so that we could go through the village of Doljani. But around half past 3.00, the fire was opened and that is where we were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, who captured you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Members of the HVO. They were mostly -- rather, no. All of them were from the village of Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How many HVO soldiers captured you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, I can't -- I can't say exactly, but I'd say there were seven or eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, you say they captured you. What does that mean? How did they capture you and what did they do after they had captured you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, when we were in the woods, some were asleep, some were sitting, and then we heard gunfire from all sides, as we were in a hollow, and then my friend was wounded, and they told us to surrender and to discard our weapons, and we did that. And then they came to us and tied us, and then I asked that we dress the wound or at least bandage the wound of this friend of mine, and they allowed us, and then we carried him down to the hamlet of Orlovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what did you find when you reached the hamlet of Orlovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We found there some soldiers too. We did not know who they were. They told to us empty our pockets. We did that, and then we set off towards the command, which was next to the church where they had their command. This used to be a fish pond once.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, at this time I'm going to ask that the Registrar show you a photograph that has been marked Exhibit 8.8, and I'm going to ask you if you recognise anything in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. That is where the HVO command was, and Mijat Tomic unit. That is where I was brought in front of this command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us in detail, as best as you remember, how were you brought to this place and what occurred as you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: They ordered us to move in a single file towards this commander, and we did. And there was waiting for us, as I learned later, Tuta and some other soldiers. But as I was the first one, he hit me in the face, and I fell, and he ordered that everybody else should go down. And then they ordered us to kiss the Croat soil and to crawl. And so we crawled until we reached a wooden something, a cow shed or a wooden hut, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said that you were struck by someone, and I want it to be clear in the record. Who is it that struck you at this place that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Later on, I learned that it was Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, were there others with Mr. Tuta at this place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, there were some other people whom I didn't know. One was a big man, a tall man, and they also beat us as we crawled, and they kicked us in the stomach and in the ribs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were there other soldiers in this place? How many people -- how many HVO people were present in this location at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, there were quite a number. I recognised the three neighbours. There was also Stipo, the driver. There must have been at least 20, as much as I dared look. But I was -- we dared not lift our heads. We had to look at the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you able to see what units any of these soldiers belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. I saw on some of the soldiers, say Bruno Busic, and others had Kaznjenicka Bojna patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you said that there was a point where you were to start crawling toward the cow shed or the hut. And at this time, I would ask you to take that photograph, Exhibit 8.8, with a pen and place a number 1 at the location where you had to start crawling. And then place a number 2 at the location of this hut or this shed that you've described.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness, the shed that you've described, is the shed itself shown in this photograph that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No, you can't see it. It's not there. It was there before, but it's gone now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you also mentioned that when you arrived at the location number 1, there was a big guy there. And I wanted to ask you if you know, if you know who that person was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know. But later on, when I saw papers later, newspapers, it could be that it was Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you didn't know who the person was at the time, however?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask the registrar to show you a document which has been marked as Exhibit 299.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's a new exhibit which has been distributed. I think it is now being presented to the Trial Chamber. The Defence has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, this is two pages, the second page of which is the document in its original Serbo-Croat language. If you just take a look at this document, I'm going to ask you two questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, any question asked of this witness in reference to a document can only mean inviting speculation. Look at the date, look at what it is about and what it says. I think this is merely -- that my learned friend is merely trying to offer this document through this witness, and now we realised who that was, I think that any answer that this witness will give can be speculation and nothing but speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Up to now, we don't know what kind of question the Prosecutor is going to ask. We will have your objections recorded in the transcript, and let us hear what Mr. Stringer is going to ask. Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, my first question about this document is whether you see the name of the person Andabak that you've mentioned in this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: My last question about this document is, moving down to the last line which appears above the signature, there's a reference to a place Sovicka Vrata. And could you tell us, if you know, what is that place and how does it relate to the events that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: It is a locality. When you go from Sovici to Risovac, there is a small gorge, and then Risovac comes. So that is the boundary of Jablanica. On this side, you have Sovici and Risovac. So it is kind of a boundary or a gate into Sovici and Risovac. And it was controlled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was this position involved in the attack on Sovici on the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Why, yes. They held it. They had the checkpoint right below it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this person that you think is Andabak, can you describe him, as best as you recall from the person you saw on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, he was big, strong built. He had glasses. But it was a long time ago, and this is more or less what comes to my mind right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Oh, no. Well, he was in a uniform, in an army uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall how Tuta was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Tuta -- at that time, Tuta had a black shirt and camouflage trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, while we are on the subject -- well, we will come back to it later. Now, you have told us about how you were hit and then you and the others were made to crawl to the location you've marked as number 2. Can you tell us then what happened after you and the others arrived at this place, location number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: When we crawled up to that place, we went up on our knees, and then he took inside the shed first Fikret Begic, then Denis Skender, and when Denis Skender came out, Tuta approached me and Fikret and said he is to put us before the firing squad because we were responsible for the death of some of his men, and he wanted to separate us from those others.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you, when you arrived with the others at this shed, what were the other soldiers present, the HVO soldiers, what were they doing as you and the others arrived at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: They walked up and down. Some were around us, striking us, ordering us to pick grapes, that is to stretch upward and then they would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. hit us in the stomach, and others again were laughing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If you could, describe for us in more detail what you mean by "picking the grapes"? Particularly how -- what was your position and how were you beaten as you were "picking the grapes"? Just so we understand what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. When we got there, they ordered us to kneel and then to reach up as if we were picking grapes, and then they beat us in the -- around the area of the stomach and rib cage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just so we are clear, who was being beaten? You say they were beating "us."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I was beaten, then my friend Amir, and the other two or three who were there with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How many altogether were in your group by this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We were nine. The six of us were captured right away, and the three of them started fleeing and they were captured a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, while this -- these beatings were taking place, this "picking of the grapes," was Tuta present while that was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No. He was inside. He was taking people inside one by one to interrogate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And where were these interrogations taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Inside the shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you know, who was the first person that was taken inside the shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: As far as I can recall -- shall I say the first and last name?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, maybe we could go into private session and I could get some of these questions out of the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned two people who went into the shed, and if you recall, can you tell us what happened after the second of those people then came out of the shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Then Tuta came out and separated me and my friend and said that he was going to have us executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what exactly, as best as you can recall, what did he say to you? How did this exchange take place? Just describe it for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: He came out of the shed, and he pointed his finger at me and my comrade and said that he would have us executed because we were to blame for the deaths of some of his men. And he looked at me in the eyes and said, "Are you afraid?" I said, "No." And then he hit me again in the face --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, then what happened after you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: -- with the Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, then what happened after you had this exchange of words with Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: He then went in the direction of the shed and went in. Then my comrade, who was with him in his unit, he came over and said, "What is this? Who is this --" and I asked, "Who is this who wants to have me shot?" And he said, "Tuta." He said, "Wait, I'll go in and see what he wants."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, now, this person that you said was your comrade, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what unit did he belong to, just so we're clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: He belonged to the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is this someone that you had known before the conflict started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, again, what is it that he said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: He asked me what I was doing there and said, "Where are you going?" And I said where -- I was living near Jablanica. And then I told him that this man wanted to have me shot. And he said, "Who?" And I didn't know who it was. And so I said, "That old man." And he said, "Oh, Tuta." And then he went over to Tuta and they talked something.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And then what happened after they had their exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Then Tuta came over to me and said -- he asked me whether I wanted to save my skin and my comrade's skin. And I said yes. And then he said, "Come on in." And the big man, Andabak, also went in with us, and then we went in. And Tuta asked me about Arif Pasilic when he was in Sovici for the last time. And I said I only saw him on television. And then he asked me about Kulja, Salem Dlakic, and I just knew that he was the battalion commander there for a while. And then he said, "Who brought you the weapons?" And I said, "They collected some money in Germany and they brought it here." And then he said, "Okay, very well. You saved your skin and of your colleagues, but if you do it again, I'll find you."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long did you remain in that shed with Tuta and the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I was there no more than ten minutes, perhaps five or six minutes all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Then I came outside. And again, I went back to picking the grapes. Then I saw my friend being beaten, and I saw blood coming out of his mouth. And as he -- then he spat it out, and then one of them said -- this German -- he said, "Can I beat the person who is spitting on the Croatian ground?" And then another soldier approached me who I asked -- he asked me whether I had sold him some appliance on Siroki Brijeg. And then he kicked me with his boot in the mouth and kicked out my two teeth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, you said --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: And I said that I did, and then he stopped beating me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, just to go back over this, a couple of questions. You made a reference to a German. Can you explain that in a little more detail, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: It was this soldier who was there. He was a German by origin, and then he said whether he could kick the person who is spitting on the Croatian blood [as interpreted], and I could understand him because I had spent six months in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So he was speaking German?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, then, can you tell us what happened then next, what happened after you exited the shed and were with the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I talked about how I was being beaten, and then Tuta came out and said, "That's enough. Stop, and take the young one and send him off with the civilians." And then they loaded us up in a vehicle and sent to Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, after you left Sovici and went to Ljubuski, did you ever see this person Tuta again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. Once he came in Mostar, in front of the prison. He opened the door to the -- I only saw him outside when he was standing there in the -- and apparently, he also just opened the door to the room where we were, peeked inside, and then left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of this prison that you're referring to in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: The Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, can you describe Tuta for us as best as you can recall from the times you saw him in Sovici, and then again at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: At that time, he had a bit longer hair in the back, and he was parting it in the middle. He also had a beard. He had glasses, roundish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you recall the colour of his hair or the colour of his beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: A greying, not completely grey, but greying. It was more white than not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Witness, let me ask you about some events that occurred when you were at the facility in Ljubuski. First of all, while you were in Ljubuski, did you ever receive any information about events that occurred in Sovici Doljani after you were removed from Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. I think the next day or two days later, somebody came and took down the names when we were going into the van. And he said that we could have been killed because Cikota, Tuta's deputy, had been killed around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at the Ljubuski -- just tell us about this place where you and the others were put in Ljubuski. Can you describe the conditions there and how long you stayed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We arrived in Ljubuski, I guess it was the central prison there before. I think that is what it was called. And we entered there in a room which measured two by something, I don't know, maybe six metres, and we called it number 6. We were between 20 and 25 in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall how long you remained at the prison in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I stayed in Ljubuski about 40 days. And then we were told that we would be exchanged, and took our name -- took down our names but then they sent us to Mostar instead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were there prisoners at Ljubuski who had come from other locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. These men were not in our room, but there were some from Prozor and some men from Mostar, and there were also two men from Ljubuski in other rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you tell us how the prisoners were treated generally by the guards at the Ljubuski prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: In Ljubuski while I was there, it wasn't -- nothing much happened. This Petrovic was the worst. He beat some people, not me, but nobody touched us. We went to work and they behaved correctly towards us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How were the men from Mostar treated, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: The men from Mostar were in another room, and I saw this Petrovic on one occasion, he was beating a man who they said was a pilot, he was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. captured in Vranica and he was beating him with a shovel and he was forcing him to say that he was a Croat, and he said that he was a Croat of Catholic faith, and I saw him beating him, as this Petrovic was beating him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know if there were other prisoners at Ljubuski who had come from Vranica in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: There were -- they said that some had been captured when we were working, that some men from Tuta's unit came and took them away in a bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, during the 40 days that you spent at Ljubuski, were you taken out of Ljubuski, the prison, to perform labour during the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. We went to work almost every day at the front lines facing the Serbs. We were digging, and I was filling sandbags, and this was towards Trebinje, towards Neum.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what were the conditions there for you and the others on the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: One had to work all day, and when the Serbs were shooting, we would take cover a little bit, but you had to work regardless of whether there was shooting going on or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you say that after you spent 40 days at the prison in Ljubuski, then what's the next place that you were taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: They took us to Mostar, to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And how long, then, did you remain at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom, I stayed until the 1st of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you permitted to take your belongings with you from Ljubuski to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. They allowed us to take the belongings that we had. We did. But when we arrived in Mostar, they took them away from us at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what sort of belongings are we talking about? What sorts of things were taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We had some clothing, which we got, I guess people from the Red Cross, and the money, watches, they took all of that away from us at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask the Registrar who is with you there to show you another photograph that's been marked Exhibit 20.10. And my question is whether you're able to recognise anything that's shown in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: As far as I can see, we were locked up here, except now there is a parking lot here. That wasn't there before. There was just a clearing there when they would take us out for fresh air.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to take that photograph with the pen and to place a circle around the building that you've just mentioned, the place where you believe you were held.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. For the record, Mr. President, the witness has placed a number 1 on the yellow building that's shown on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, can you describe for us generally the conditions that you and the others were held in, the conditions there that existed in this building during the months that you were held there? I'm talking about space, sleeping room, food, toilet facilities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: When we arrived at the Heliodrom, at first we weren't that many, and we had some military cots there. But some other men were brought in, and then all that was taken out, and we were given two blankets each. I was in the room where we were over 100. And we had -- we were receiving food in the morning, and we had an evening meal. We would get tea and a slice of bread. On one occasion, I had to slice a loaf, and I had to slice it -- and I had to divide it into 11 pieces. And that is what we were getting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is that generally the amount of food that you would receive during a meal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What about the sleeping arrangements? You said the cots were removed, so where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I slept on the floor. I had a blanket underneath, and we were in three rows. I think it was -- the room measured 6 by 10 metres, and I believe that we were over 100. And then we had a person who was in charge of the room, and he had to give the count of the people in the room to the policeman on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you receive any beatings while you were being held at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. They beat us. I personally was beaten about ten times, and also at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you describe for us just in general terms the type of beatings that you received while you were in the Heliodrom complex?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I can give you an example. Once I was beaten with truncheons, and I was being kicked and a commander placed a pistol in his mouth and cocked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: He placed a pistol in whose mouth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: My mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, just a moment ago, you mentioned that you were also beaten at the front line. Did you go out from the Heliodrom at various --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- times? Did you go out from the Heliodrom, you and others, to work at various front-line positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, we went to Grude -- we went to Santiceva Street, Bulevar, and then towards the airport towards Dracevice, and then we went up to Breznice also.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How often during the months that you were at the Heliodrom were you taken out to perform labour at these various locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: People went every day. I went several times. I was beaten several times, and then they would spare me a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when you were taken out for forced labour, do you know what people or what units you were working for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I knew some, and I didn't know some others. But where we worked towards Dracevice, there were the 7th and the 9th battalion there. And there was an elementary school, the 3rd or the 4th. And we were told that these were Stela's men. That's where we were working. I did not know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet a person known to you as Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the Bulevar. What sorts of work, what tasks did you perform at the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: There we had to carry sandbags, make screens, dig trenches, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And how were the conditions at the Bulevar when you worked there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, none. You work, keep silent. They give you a little bit of bread to eat. And then a soldier comes up, ill treats you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask the registrar to show you a photograph that has been marked Exhibit 14.3. I'm going to ask you to look at that and tell us if you recognise any of the places shown on this photograph. Okay, Witness, let me ask you a couple questions before you make any more marks on the photograph. First, could we put the photograph on the projector, please, so that those of us here in The Hague can see it. Is it possible to see the -- okay. Witness, let me first ask you about this photograph. Do you recognise any of the locations where you worked as shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's what I would like you to do is, first, without making any marks, just use the pen and to point to the areas that you worked in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Witness, here in The Hague, we're not able to see the mark that you placed. Can you point to the place where you made the mark just a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, you're pointing to a place right now. Let me ask you to put the letter A in that place, if you would do that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you tell us what was your task, what was your job, when you were working in that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We had to carry those sandbags, to protect windows and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when you were working in that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: And to dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you were working in that location, do you know who or what unit you were working for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Not then. Later on, some pals of mine told me that he saw Stela there and that his men were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you work on any other occasions in this area that's shown on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I was there only once or twice, I can't remember exactly. Twice, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume at 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Mr. Krsnik, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me introduce myself. I represent the accused here, Mr. Mladen Naletilic. And let me give you a couple of pieces of advice and a request. Since we speak the same language, will you please listen to me until I'm done asking my question and then answer? This is for the sake of the interpreters, to make their job easier. Second, I'm going to frame my question in such a way as to get the most specific and shortest answers possible. Did you understand my request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So let's start. Let me first show you the photograph which has been shown to you a little while ago by my learned colleague, my learned friend. This is Exhibit 8.8, and we will try to work with it in order to clarify some points. Witness, my first question to you is: In this photograph, can you see the location where you were taken prisoner? In other words, from which direction did you get there to the shed which you described? If you can see it, can you please show it to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What you're showing now, you were captured there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No. I was brought there, I was led that way, but where I was taken prisoner is not in the picture, cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And can you see the direction from which you came? That is was it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to the left, from the right, from down, from closer or far?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: All the way out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can we say that it was at the foot of the mountain that we see in the background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: But on the other side, but it's at the same level as the mountain is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you at the top of the mountain or had you come down the mountain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No. I was never up there where you were. No, we were down in a -- on the lower ground, in the bed of a creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, are you talking to someone? Let us try to find another picture from which we can see better what we are looking for. While we are looking at it, what time was it when you were captured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: About 3.30, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: 3.30 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what time was it when you were brought to the shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We were brought perhaps 15, 20 minutes later, right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: 15 to 20 minutes. Were you all armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to place another photograph here. I think you will see it. And perhaps you can show it on this picture, provided you can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can ask the -- it's 8.2 for the registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you see the picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Where we are, we have Exhibit 8.3. In other words, you need to place your exhibit in the -- on the ELMO in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dubuisson, we did place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Now we can see it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, can you see it now? Approximately, the approximately the direction in which you were walking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We were moving from -- on the other side of the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: From the side of the Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I'm unable to follow you. Do you see the road bisecting the picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let's take that direction of the road. Did you move along that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No, not at all. We were not on that side at all. We were on the other side, on the side of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean on the other side of the hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you were on the other side of the hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean you were already in the Prozor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, where I was taken prisoner, that could have already been part of the Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So tell me, please, were you captured on the other side of the hill, or did you go down towards Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We went down to the lower ground near Doljani in the direction -- it was down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And why did you not continue towards Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We were waiting for the nightfall, because we wanted to move during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't understand. Why did you not continue in the direction of Jablanica where you were, I mean on the other side of the hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Because we did not know the terrain there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you said that you were all armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This entire group, 9 or 11 of you, however many you said you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you offer any resistance while withdrawing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you offer any resistance when these soldiers -- when these HVO soldiers approached?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Weren't you more than they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: They may have been, but we were in lower ground, and one of our comrade was wounded right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean they immediately opened fire on you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me: Do you remember the statement you gave to the investigators in The Hague in 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you recall that you did not offer resistance because some among you were asleep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, some were asleep. And we did not offer resistance, and we did not have time. And this comrade was immediately wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Listen: You were 11; you said that 7 HVO soldiers took you prisoner. Were you all armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: We were 11. 2 went away, and then they never came back. And we were 9 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So shooting started, and you did not offer resistance because some people were asleep while the shooting was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, this happened when those two were already some distance away from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. The HVO that took you prisoner were from Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it the Mijat Tomic battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the command, was that the Mijat Tomic battalion command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. I believe that the Trial Chamber has gained a picture how you reached that headquarters, that command post. Now, tell me, were there ABiH troops on the high ground in the direction of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: At the time when we were captured?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where did the Jablanica Brigade positions start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I was not at Jablanica at the time. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: At that time you were not in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you not sleep at your uncle's and come to Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. But at that time, there was no war. There was no shooting, and I was not a member of that battalion to know where they were going to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You were a member of the ABiH; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, I guess that is what they called it. It was the Territorial Defence first, and then it was renamed into army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you not part of a brigade, this unit from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. There was -- the brigade headquarters was at Neretva. We were only the 4th Battalion, and there were another three battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And as part of this brigade, did you not have communication with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: That was not my job. I was a regular soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you, Mr. Dubuisson, to go back to the picture -- I think it was 8. -- could be 8.8. The picture we showed before this picture, that is, of the picture where the headquarters is shown. No, Mr. Dubuisson, 8.8. The one we had just before the last one. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, the soldiers who took you prisoner led you and brought you where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: First they stopped at another point, and then they brought us to the Mijat Tomic headquarters at the fish pond.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who was that who brought you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: These were the soldiers from that -- from Doljani with some other unknown soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you show me now where exactly you were brought?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: They brought us right here. This is where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where did you see the man whom you called "Tuta" for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Here where the number "1" is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many men were there with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I know that there were three or four there with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you said to the Prosecutor that there were altogether about 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: As far as I could count. We couldn't even raise our heads there, so I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me where that big man was whom you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: He was there with Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And this big man, did he have a beard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No, at that time he did not have a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, do you remember how many statements you've given until today's evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember giving a statement to the security service in Jablanica in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I have given statements, I don't know to whom, but I think I also gave one in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The statement that you gave in 1997, where did you give that statement to the investigators from The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In Sarajevo. And did they show you some pictures there, in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And do you remember when you last spoke with the representatives of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: In January of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: At that time, in January of this year, did you sign a statement under oath?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In that statement, you said that everything that you had stated in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. those previous two statements to the security service and the one you gave in Sarajevo are completely and absolutely truth. You remember having sworn to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. I remember reading the one that I gave in 1997, but I don't remember reading the one in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then why did you not say at that time, that is in January, that was in January of 2001, that means less than about ten months ago, why did you not say then that this big man was Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know. It did not cross my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know that in no statement you mention his name, ever, and you testified under oath?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when did it cross your mind that this could have been Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: It crossed my mind when I saw him first in the newspapers, and this -- it was only recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Recently? When was this recently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you talk recently with somebody from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when was this, the last time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know. It could be a month or 20 days ago. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into the private session for one question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in which newspaper did you see the man whom you recognised as Andabak and where and when was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: It was while I was in Bosnia but I also buy newspapers like Globus and Oslobodenje here as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And in which year did you see his picture in Oslobodenje? I'm not going to ask you the months.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Here, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I think it was in 1999 or 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't know the month, even approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: How can I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What about Globus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You saw it there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And this was in 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when you gave the statement, no one ever showed you his pictures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Not The Hague investigators, neither the security services?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How about Tuta's pictures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Again, no one ever showed you pictures that I just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I think you still have that picture in front of you. Where were you when Tuta allegedly hit you, and why would he hit you? Why did he hit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: You mean the first time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes. Here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: You mean where --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please be advised not to interrupt the witness and wait and pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean that is a Motorola or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where did he hit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: In the face, on the cheek, the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Which part of the head?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I missed the last couple of lines of translation, I believe, and I'm not seeing it either on the television --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We had asked for the counsel to be advised to please mind the breaks between questions and answers. They are running into each other, and it is impossible to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The interpreter asked us to advise you not to interrupt the witness and wait and pause between question and answers. We missed certain parts of the answer from this witness. I know it's a late hour, but you have plenty time. I can guarantee you about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. You are very kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You see, Witness TT, unfortunately we have to go back for these past two or three questions because they are not in the record. So I will do it slowly, and you do it slowly please, too. All right? All right. I heard your answer but the interpreters did not. Which part of the head were you struck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: He hit me on the cheek, part of my cheek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Which cheek, right or left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It's when you were standing, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, I fell then, and then we were all ordered to lie down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. I see. You fell. Just a moment, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I think we missed an answer from the witness. Your question is that where were you when Tuta allegedly hit you, and why would he hit you? Why did he hit you? We missed the answer to this question. You may ask this question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours. I think we have already learned where he was because he showed it on the photograph, next to number 1 on the photograph. The witness answered that, and I believe my learned friend can confirm it. But we did not hear the answer as to why.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, I will ask you again. Why did he hit you like that out of the blue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know why. As soon as we arrived there, he started cursing and hitting us. As I was the first one in the line, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dubuisson, could you please give the witness the statement that you gave, that you gave to The Hague investigators in Sarajevo. I mean the statement of 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, will you please turn to page 5, the last sentence. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'll read it out to you, and you listen now to me. "We were ordered to lie down on the ground in front of the building. And as we were lying down, I heard someone say to Denis, 'Young boy, young man, come with me.'" It is page 7 of the English version. Now, please turn the next page. "And while we were lying down with our faces to the ground, Tuta had a Motorola in his hand. And in one moment, while I was kneeling, he hit me in the face with this Motorola." Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, you see it's completely different from what you told us today. Somebody else ordered you to lie down, and you were already lying down. And in this statement, you say how you were kneeling. You told us today a completely different story, how you arrived; and no sooner than you arrived, then Tuta -- so tell me what is the truth? What you said in the statement, or what you told us today? And please will you wait for me to finish my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the, my view, as a mischaracterisation of what the statement says. The statement, as read, says, "We were ordered to lay down on the ground ..." and continues. What counsel now has just said is that somebody else ordered you to lay down. The statement does not say whether it was Tuta or someone else who ordered them to lay down, and I would just ask that counsel be very careful as to how he characterises the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there any problem with the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I ask my learned friend to read this together. I cannot be responsible for this translation, if my translation -- if this translation says what he did not say. But in my version, in Croat, it says, They ordered or we were ordered. That is plural. We were ordered, again, plural, to lie down on the ground. So can the interpreters be given that so we can compare this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. because I do not see what is in dispute here. It says, plural, We were ordered, or they ordered us to lie down. "They", two plurals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The booth has -- I know that the B/C/S to English booth -- I'm sorry, the English to B/C/S booth has both versions, and I think it's irrelevant because I think that as it has been read by counsel, I think that they are exactly identical; that is, "We were ordered to lay down." And that's exactly how it came back to me from counsel's language into my language. "We," plural, being the prisoners, "we were ordered" -- that's a passive impersonal use of the verb, "We were ordered to lay down." It continues: "I heard someone saying to Denis, young boy, come with me." So my only point, Mr. President, is that rather than arguing with the witness about what the statement does or does not say, I think that the statement really should be read clearly and accurately, and that suggestions should not be put to the witness which are inconsistent with what is, indeed, in both languages versions of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I'm afraid we all heard the same way as Mr. Stringer put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, will you please hear me out? My words are distorted, and an attempt is made to distort what I have in my version in the Croatian language, and it says very clearly, not "that" but "those who are ordering." Not only "prisoners" are in the plural. It says in the Croatian language, "And they ordered us to lie down on the ground." So it is a number of people ordered "us" to lie down. So I hope my learned friend will not be helping the witness out, because the witness said today, "when I came -- when I fetched up in front of the building, I was hit," but here in the statement, he says they were already lying down on the ground because somebody else had ordered them to lie down on the ground. Besides, we have both statements here and we can compare them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask the registrar to ask the interpreters to check the translations over the night. And the registrar will file a report on the translations. Would you please move on, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I shall immediately provide those statements. If Madam Registrar does not have them, I have them here. So will you please help me with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, were you lying down on the ground when Tuta hit you, or did he hit you because you were the first one in this file, as you said today, and when you approached him, and then you fell on the ground, because you were struck? That is what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I said as far as I can remember. It was a long time ago. Why didn't you ask me the first year? At that time I knew everything, but I said that as I came up, he hit me, and then he ordered me to lie down. Now, I don't know how this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, was your memory better in 1997 or today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know, sorry, I don't. All I know is that he hit me as I was walking up to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, I'm asking you, Witness, what is right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: What I said today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And this sentence in the statement, that is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, this is also correct, except that I just don't know -- I don't know exactly how I put it then. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Now, let's move on, Witness TT. First, tell me, please, what is the name of the man -- and please don't shuffle those papers in front of the microphone because we are here getting very bad noise indeed. Thank you. Will you tell us, what is the name of the man who allegedly saved you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not getting any bad noise, and that's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, because you are listening to the English channel, and I believe that Mr. Krsnik is on the B/C/S channel, I think that's the difference. That's no point for interruption, Mr. Stringer. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you for the full name of that person and a description of the man who saved you from the alleged execution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I do not know his full name. I have known the man for a long time. We've always called him Janos, and I knew where he lived. We socialised and would have drinks together on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please repeat that name once again, and spell it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Janos. We called him Janos, and I don't know his name, either his first or his last name, J-a-n-o-c -- n-o-s, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you describe him for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. He was a young man of about 30, 35, 36, sturdy, his hair was shortly cut.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And where he came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: He was from Jablanica, from Gornji Kolonija. I know all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you've known him for a long time, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was he a commander of sorts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, who told you to pick the grapes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, one -- Tuta told us to kneel down and then somebody else came and said that we should reach upward and make as if we were picking the grapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But you do not know what the man looks like or who that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, did you ever see -- you mentioned today that name. Did you ever see Cikota?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No. But when we arrived in Ljubuski, we saw him in the newspapers, and I remember he was fair-haired and tall, had a scarf around his neck, and that is the picture exactly that we saw in the newspapers after we arrived in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I should like to ask Mr. Dubuisson to show the witness his statement that he gave to the security service on the 29th of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please look at the first page, the first page where it says "Statement," and now look at the one, two, three, four, sixth passage? I will read it to you. "Two foreigners were with Tuta, and I heard about them, that they were Germans. And a man nicknamed Cikota, who was blond, stocky, had short hair, was about 25 years old, and also wore a black scarf around his neck." Then why did you tell the security -- the state security service that you saw him if, as you confirmed to us today, you said that you never saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, I saw him that day, but I didn't know that it was Cikota until we saw him in the newspaper in Ljubuski after he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sir, let us read once again what you said. My question to you was: Did you ever see the person whom you mentioned today? A minute ago you told us that you hadn't.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I did see him that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness TT, but you said that you saw him in the newspaper when you arrived in Ljubuski, and here you state quite clearly, I mean in 1995, that you had seen him and you described him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That was it, but I didn't know -- I didn't associate the man with the name Cikota until we saw it in the newspaper at Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And in 1995, you asserted this, and immediately said -- and immediately told about that to the state security people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
