utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the counsel begins to speak before the witness finishes his answer, and we who are listening to the French are really overwhelmed by the speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour. I shall do my best not to do it again. I'm very sorry. And I'll turn to the French channel to listen, to see when they finish so that I can then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What time was it -- what time was it when you were put in the van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. I don't remember what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But roughly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, I do not know roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it at dusk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was dusk. Yes, it was getting dark. And at the time when we crossed to Risovac, yes, the night had already fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you are sure that it was the 24th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mentioned today that you had heard somebody tell you that Cikota had been killed and that it happened at the time when you were there. Had it happened at the time when you were there, that you would have been executed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: That's right, because the men who took our names as we were entering the van, our full names, and he said that had you stayed here an hour longer, you would have been all killed because Cikota had got killed, Tuta's deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you ever learn whether he was killed, when that happened, and whether he was killed at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know. That is what they said, and there was this obituary in the newspaper saying that he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This man who took your names down who told you that, was he a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: An HVO military policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, he had that white belt in his trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And he was the one who took your names down and put you in the van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We entered the van, and then they drove us away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And escorted by him -- or rather, escorted by the military police, you went to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not see that man come with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But it was military police no doubt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And all nine of you were put in this Volkswagen van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No. Denis was taken to the school. He wasn't with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: As a matter of fact he was released, he was set free, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Not set free. He was sent to the school to join other civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's your assumption. You do not know that, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Counsel invited that speculation by his last question, and I think that he should not criticise the answer that he received from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree with you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Krsnik, skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, if a witness goes in one direction, then how can we know where the other man went? Why should it be speculation? It is the witness who is making speculations, not me. But whatever. I'll withdraw that question. Doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where exactly in Ljubuski were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: To the central prison. That is what they call them. I don't know. I mean, it's for those who know Ljubuski well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you have your statement of 1995? Page 2. You said you were put in the police station in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where there were many detainees, many other detainees.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, sure, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you visited by a commissioner of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, they did, but I wasn't there at the time. I was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you take that statement, look at it. One passage down. You say here that you were present. "We were also visited by a joint commission of the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't say I was present there. When I returned, others told me they had been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then you continue: "... who showed interest in our living conditions, whether we were being beaten, and the detainees amongst us who had been killed." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: It is true. I heard about that when I came back from work. I was not there, and I did not say I was there when I was giving this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness TT, please, truly, will you please wait for me to finish my question. You see, I've switched to another language to enable everybody, because the interpreters have difficulties to follow you. Will you please wait. When I finish my question, then you can give us your answer slowly. Thank you. So you were not present when this commission arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know for sure that they were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: That is what my fellow prisoners told me when I came back from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were physicians part of that commission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I believe -- but I think that Alija Zujo [phoen] was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness says he was not present when the commission came, so it seems that your next question is totally irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps you're right. I don't know whether it is relevant, but it's interesting to hear that Ljubuski was visited by the commission of the ABiH, and I believe that there are records about it, and I'm glad that the witness mentioned it. It was a mixed, joint commission, that had physicians, aid workers and all kinds of things. I think it's not bad to hear that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what the witness said is clear, "That was what my fellow prisoners told me when I came back from work," and he was not there, so how could he confirm whether there is a physician there or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour. However, in his statement, he said - that is in Croatian version, which can be compared to the English version, obviously - he was there. This is why I asked the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, tell me, what was your treatment in Ljubuski like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I said that in Ljubuski we received food twice a day, we went to perform labour, nobody touched us. Personally, myself, I myself was not touched, and most other prisoners also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you see anyone being beaten in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I did. I saw it, but I saw this one policeman who worked there doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you be so kind as to take your statement from 1997? Please turn to page 7. It would be the last paragraph. I will read slowly: "During our stay in the prison, they were quite correct to us. That is during our stay in central prison. As far as I could see, nobody was beaten and everything was correct."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. As far as we were concerned, nobody touched us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Nor did you ever see that anyone was beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, I did see that somebody was beaten, when Petrovic beat one of our -- one of our fellow prisoners, but it was somebody from Mostar. These were not one of the men who were from our area. And also some from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Why didn't you say so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, nobody asked us. They asked me -- you asked me whether I was -- we were beaten, and that means we who were brought there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Here, you state expressly, "They did not beat anyone."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: From among those of us who had arrived in the first group, nobody was beaten. But we could see when they were beating someone when we went to get our meals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the commander, was he also correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: As far as I was concerned, he was, and I did not see him mistreat anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That was also military police, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the guards in Ljubuski also belonged to the military police, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: They had those white belts, so I'm sure they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And at the Heliodrom, that was also the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when these work details were formed, who from the outside would come, or to receive the humanitarian organisations and so on, who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know. There were guards there, and then Ante Smiljanic was there. I think he was the man in charge. And then after a while, there were people who were sort of the heads of the room, and they were the ones who would decide who was going to go, and that went on for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In your statement, on page 8, if you will turn over to page 8, please, you say - that was the fourth from the bottom -- excuse me, fifth. I'm sorry, you do not assert. You say, "I think that Ante Smiljanic was the commander of the camp. He was a military police officer, and he was the one whom everyone asked about things. So I assume that he was the commander." Then you go on to say this: "When someone would come from outside in order to perform work details, they would always ask him. And the same went for the international organisations. When they would come to the Heliodrom, they would always first contact him." My question to you, sir, is do you assert this or is this your assumption?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I saw that personally. I saw when he talked to them. And when we worked, if we were to go to the same place -- if we needed to go back to the same place, they would say we will talk to Ante before anyone else takes you to go along with them, that you will come with us to that same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I'm referring to Smiljanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, are you sure that Tuta -- you personally saw him at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You personally saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, through the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you saw him entering your building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, he was headed in the direction of the door. Then I didn't see him any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And in your building, were there any HVO soldiers who were serving sentences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, at first there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you to please take your mind back to Sovici. Will you please say what types of uniforms did the soldiers who arrested you wear and in front of that shed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: There were both black and camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know who was wearing black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know to which unit did this soldier belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I could only know that by their patches on their sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We said that you knew that this was the Mijat Tomic battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And those in black uniforms, were they perhaps members of the HOS, the HOS units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know. It is possible that they were wearing black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you said that you knew that the Convicts Battalion was there Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. because you saw their insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Of this patch was on the chest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No, on the sleeve. I saw it on the sleeve.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where, where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Here, at around the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you see where I'm showing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, on the left or right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Fine. How did that patch look?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: It had Convicts Battalion written on it, and it had -- I don't have a clear picture of it. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when did you see that, when you were brought in front of the shed, or at a time when you were captured, or when you were boarding the van? Because you were either lying on the ground or you had your head down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Well, where I turned, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you also noticed this other unit. What did you say its name was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Bruno Busic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, please, how did their patch look, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, when you gave that interview in Sarajevo, did they ask you questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Some, I think they did, but I don't recall it any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did they show you various patches of various HVO units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No unit was suggested to you, no name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into the private session, please, for one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please. Wait, wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Your unit in Sovici did not get support by anyone from Jablanica or the surrounding areas? You did not get any supporting manpower?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you who were there were there and nobody ever came to help you or to replenish your ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: During the conflict, some men came from Visnjani, and I think there were also two men from Doljani at one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how many managed to escape? You did not on that day, but on the 17th, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know how many escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, the man who you said got wounded, he also went with you to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes. We bandaged him, and then at Doljani someone re-bandaged him, and then he came with us to Ljubuski. Some physicians bandaged him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And my last question: What year was it when you saw Tuta? Is it possible that it was 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Where? You mean in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't know that exactly. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may just consult with my team to see if I missed anything? Thank you, Witness, for your patience. I hope that you have helped us all. Your Honours, this was my last question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric, do you have any cross-examination? Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just one or two questions. It will depend on how long it will take.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness TT, today you said that you performed labour with the 3rd or 4th elementary school at Sam Stela [phoen] in the statement that you gave and which was shown and which you have in front of, on the 26th of April, 1997, that is. If you turn to page 10, you will see that in the second paragraph, you said this: "I heard from other prisoners that other work details had worked for a man called Stela." And then the paragraph after that, and that's the last sentence "I have never heard anything special regarding labour for Stela." Can you now interpret for me how come you stated what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: At that time, I did not know that I had worked there. But my fellow prisoners told me that Stela was in charge of there. I never saw Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. him so I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let me take you back. You said this verbatim: "I heard from other prisoners that other work details had worked for a man called Stela." And then you added, "I have never heard anything special about labour for Stela."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: That is correct. I only worked once or twice there. I did not know that Stela was there. I heard from others who were going there later. I was among the first who went there. But there were others who were there working for him nonstop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And if I told you that this Stela of whom you had never heard was not a commander of that segment of the front line around that school, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know what I was told who was there in charge where I was working. But I don't know anything else about Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that we see the light at the end of the tunnel. So here I have a proposal to put to all of you. Are we going to continue for a little bit longer for the sitting, or we break for the supper and resume at 8.00? Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have a maximum of two questions for redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we'll sit a little bit longer, but I was advised that the interpreters could not be with us more than two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, what I have is one point that was raised on the cross, which I think I can deal with swiftly, and I'll be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, during the cross-examination during the counsel for Mr. Naletilic, you were taken to various parts of the witness statement that you gave to the investigators of the OTP in April of 1997. And I want to direct your attention to one part -- actually two parts of that witness statement. And if you would take the version of that witness statement, which is in B/C/S, I would like to direct your attention to one part of it. And I believe it may have been on page 7 of your version; the sentence that reads as follows: "During our stay in central prison, they were very correct to us. Nobody was beaten as far as I could see, and everything was correct." Do you find that sentence in the B/C/S version which you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: First question. When you said "they were correct to us", who are you referring to when you said "us"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: I'm referring to us, specifically our group which went to work. I mean, mostly us from Sovici; that is, us, we who were captured in the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, during the cross-examination, counsel told you that you did not say anything about the beating you saw of Hasib Lulic who was from Mostar. Do you remember him telling you that you said nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I never once mentioned any name, and especially the name of the gentleman mentioned by my learned friend. So could this question be withdrawn. I did not go beyond those two sentences, and there my cross-examination about Ljubuski and the treatment in Ljubuski ended. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, did you give the fair characterisation of what counsel said?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I did, Mr. President. I prefer not to withdraw the question. I think that counsel -- that this witness testified about a beating he saw. He told the trial Chamber who was beaten and where he was from, and counsel challenged the witness by asserting that he did not describe that beating in his witness statement. And I would like to now direct the witness to a different part of his witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I will say only one thing. What the learned friend is saying is simply not true, and that is so. I read one sentence and asked if it was true, and the witness answered very simply. I do not think that my memory fails me because it happened some ten minutes ago. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can we clear it up? Was Mr. Lulic the pilot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he was not. It was somebody else from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, did you find that paragraph? We are waiting for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, the paragraph in the witness statement, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. I mean in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If it's any assistance, Mr. Stringer, I think it's around page 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm looking at page 53 of the transcript, line 7. The question is: "Nor did you ever see anyone that was beaten?" The witness then describes a beating by someone named Petrovic. Counsel says, "Why didn't you say so?" And that is the matter I would like to follow up on by directing the witness to a different part of his witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness explained it all very nicely. When I asked him, he never mentioned a single name. He simply said, later on, that he saw a guard called Petrovic beat somebody. I think the transcript says it all very nicely. And I said that, "This is not in your statement. You claimed that you never saw anyone being beaten." And that is what the discussion was about, and not who. So it's all very simple. I don't see why these things are being complicated now, because we never mentioned any names. Let me complete it. The discussion was about whether he did see or didn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, I believe your question is further away from the question put forward by Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I respectfully disagree. Counsel's impeached this witness by referring to a selected portion of a witness statement. He ignored a different section, passage, which is merely one paragraph down in the statement, which in my view would rehabilitate the witness on this particular point, which counsel expressly tried to impeach his credibility on. Counsel's point was that this witness saw no beatings, and the witness has tried to explain that, in fact, he did see a beating. And I would now attempt to draw the witness's attention to a different portion of the witness statement, very close to the one counsel has relied on, selectively, in my view, in order to give this witness an opportunity to demonstrate to the Trial Chamber that, in fact, as he said to Mr. Krsnik, he did try to -- he did, in fact, describe the beating that he saw. Counsel in the transcript says that, "You expressly "-- that he expressly didn't say it, and, in fact, I'm trying to demonstrate that that is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, why don't you pose your question another way by reading the paragraphs in the previous statement so that we could have overall picture of that previous statement? Because we don't have those statements at our hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That was my intention. So now I would ask the witness to look again at the statement. And from the sentence which we just read together which begins with the words, "During our stay," I would like the witness to move down, to skip the next paragraph and move down to the paragraph which begins with the words, "Also the guards."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you if this is what your statement says in that paragraph: "Also the guards in the prison were from the military police. I know that one of the guards were called Petrovic, who used to beat some of the prisoners. I saw once that he was beating Hasib Lulic with his fist in his face while we were on our way to our meal. He was hit twice in the face." Now, Witness, was that the beating that you were referring to during your cross-examination that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS TT
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness, for coming to help us by giving your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender into evidence? Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we tender Exhibit 8.8, as marked, which is now Exhibit 8.8/2; Exhibit 20.10, as marked, which is now 20.10/2; and Exhibit 14.3, as marked, which is now 14.3/6. At this time, also, we would tender the document which the witness referred to during his direct marked as Exhibit 199.1 -- I'm sorry, 299.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As usual, we have no objections to those exhibits on which -- when these exhibits are photographs marked by witnesses. But Your Honours, to offer documents in such a way, I mean, there were thousands of documents with the names -- with the name of Ivan Andabak, other documents, newspaper articles. And again, we have another document, once again, without seal, without anything. We do not know the source, where, from, why, whence this document. So of course we object to this document, 299.1. If need be, we shall do it in writing within eight days; perhaps even sooner than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Those documents of the maps and photographs marked by the witness are admitted into evidence. As for the Document P299.1, we will await your written response in seven days. Mr. Seric? No. Thank you very much. Are there any documents on the Defence counsel's side to be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we'll resume our hearings with the previous witness tomorrow morning at 9.30 a.m.
